name: Mamprusi Kingdom
description: The Mamprusi Kingdom was an indigenous West African monarchy established in the fertile savanna basin of northern Ghana, governed by a paramount ruler titled the Nayiri. In 1899, amid fierce Anglo-French competition for control over the upper Volta hinterland, the kingdom entered into a short-lived protectorate agreement with French colonial authorities based at Gambaga. This diplomatic alignment proved fleeting, as bilateral European boundary accords in 1900 recognised the region as falling within the British sphere of influence, ending French oversight. \n\n Status: Protectorate of France; Capital: Gambaga; Common languages: Mampruli and French; Religion: Traditional African religion and Sunni Islam; Government: Traditional kingdom under colonial protectorate; Historical era: Scramble for Africa; Established: 1899; Disestablished: 1900; Succeeded by: Mamprusi Kingdom (German protectorate)

name: Sheikhdom of Kuwait
description: The Sheikhdom of Kuwait was a maritime Arab realm located at the north-western tip of the Persian Gulf, governed by the Al Sabah dynasty. In January 1899, Sheikh Mubarak Al-Sabah concluded an exclusive protection treaty with Great Britain to prevent Ottoman annexation and secure British maritime supremacy. Developing from a prosperous pearling and boatbuilding harbour into a major petroleum exporter in the mid-twentieth century, Kuwait maintained British protected state status until gaining full sovereign independence on 19 June 1961. \n\n Status: British protected state; Capital: Kuwait City; Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Kuwaiti Arabic and English; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Hereditary sheikhdom; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 23 January 1899; Disestablished: 19 June 1961; Succeeded by: State of Kuwait

name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland and United States of America (Military Occupation)
description: The joint military occupation by the United Kingdom and the United States refers to the combined Anglo-American naval and ground command established in Samoa during the Second Samoan Civil War. Initiated in March 1899, Allied warships bombarded rival factions around Apia in support of King Malietoa Tanumafili I against German-backed combatants. The joint military oversight maintained martial control until the ratification of the Tripartite Convention in February 1900, which partitioned the Samoan archipelago between the United States and Imperial Germany. \n\n Status: Joint military occupation zone; Administrative seat: Apia; Common languages: English and Samoan; Religion: Protestantism and Roman Catholicism; Government: Joint naval military administration; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 30 March 1899; Disestablished: 16 February 1900; Succeeded by: German Samoa and American Samoa

name: Republic of Cuba
description: The Republic of Cuba under United States protectorate encompasses the early constitutional eras during which Cuban sovereignty was heavily constrained by the Platt Amendment. Governed from Havana, the republic maintained elected civilian institutions but conceded extensive American rights of military intervention, economic supervision and naval leases at Guantanamo Bay. Despite repeated foreign occupations and political instability, this quasi-protectorate framework persisted until the abrogation of the Platt Amendment in June 1934 under the Good Neighbour Policy. \n\n Status: Constitutional republic under American protectorate; Capital: Havana; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Presidential republic under treaty protectorate; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 11 April 1899; Disestablished: 9 June 1934; Preceded by: United States Military Government in Cuba; Succeeded by: Republic of Cuba

name: Republic of Zamboanga
description: The Republic of Zamboanga was a revolutionary maritime state founded on 28 May 1899 on the south-western tip of Mindanao in the southern Philippines. Proclaimed by General Vicente Álvarez after his revolutionary forces captured the Spanish stronghold of Fort Pilar, the republic established an elected chamber of deputies and asserted sovereignty over the Zamboanga peninsula. The revolutionary regime fiercely resisted invading United States forces before internal fractures and American military incursions ended its autonomous existence in early 1903. \n\n Status: Unrecognised revolutionary republic; Capital: Zamboanga City; Common languages: Chavacano, Spanish and Tagalog; Religion: Roman Catholicism and Sunni Islam; Government: Revolutionary presidential republic; Historical era: Philippine-American War; Established: 28 May 1899; Disestablished: 1 April 1903; Succeeded by: Insular Government of the Philippine Islands

name: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan
description: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan was an expansive colonial condominium established across the upper Nile basin following the reconquest of the Mahdist state by British and Egyptian forces. Formally constituted under the Condominium Agreement of June 1899, administrative authority was vested in a Governor-General in Khartoum appointed with Egyptian consent but effectively controlled by the British government. The administration consolidated imperial rule over diverse northern Muslim and southern African populations, constructing extensive railway and irrigation schemes until twentieth-century nationalist transformations. \n\n Status: Condominium of Great Britain and Egypt; Capital: Khartoum; Official languages: English and Arabic; Common languages: Sudanese Arabic, Dinka, Nuer, Nubian and Beja; Religion: Sunni Islam, Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Colonial condominium; Historical era: New Imperialism; Established: 19 June 1899; Disestablished: 1925; Succeeded by: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan (reorganised)

name: Independent State of Acre
description: The Independent State of Acre was a secessionist republic proclaimed in the dense Amazonian rainforests of the disputed upper Purús river basin. Founded in July 1899 by Brazilian rubber tappers under the leadership of Spanish journalist Luis Gálvez Rodríguez, the unrecognised state sought independence from Bolivian customs control and extraction taxes. Following repeated armed insurgencies against Bolivian expeditionary forces, the conflict culminated in military victory under José Plácido de Castro and the formal incorporation of Acre into Brazil. \n\n Status: Unrecognised secessionist republic; Capital: Porto Acre; Official languages: Portuguese and Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Revolutionary presidential republic; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 14 July 1899; Disestablished: 7 April 1904; Preceded by: Republic of Bolivia; Succeeded by: Acre Federal Territory

name: South African Republic and Orange Free State (Military Occupation)
description: The joint military occupation by the South African Republic and Orange Free State designates the initial offensive campaigns launched by allied Boer commandos during the Second Boer War. Invading the British colonies of Natal and the Cape in October 1899, Boer forces established military governance over captured frontier towns, including the siege sectors of Ladysmith, Mafeking and Kimberley. The occupation collapsed in late 1900 when overwhelming British imperial counter-offensives captured Bloemfontein and Pretoria, driving the Boers into prolonged guerrilla warfare. \n\n Status: Military occupation zone under allied Boer forces; Administrative seat: Mobile commando headquarters; Common languages: Afrikaans, Dutch and English; Religion: Dutch Reformed Church; Government: Combined Boer military administration; Historical era: Second Boer War; Established: 13 October 1899; Disestablished: 3 September 1900; Succeeded by: British Military Administration in South Africa

name: Militia United in Righteousness
description: The Militia United in Righteousness, widely known as the Boxers, was an anti-foreign and anti-Christian peasant insurgency that swept across northern China during the late Qing dynasty. Originating in rural Shandong as a martial arts movement committed to expelling Western influence and restoring dynastic prestige, the militia gained tacit support from Empress Dowager Cixi and occupied Beijing in 1900. Besieging foreign legations and destroying missionary stations, the movement was decisively crushed when the multinational Eight-Nation Alliance captured the imperial capital. \n\n Status: Popular insurgent movement; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Mandarin Chinese; Religion: Chinese folk religion, Buddhism and Taoism; Government: Decentralised militia councils; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 18 October 1899; Disestablished: 7 September 1901; Succeeded by: Qing Dynasty

name: Barotziland-North-Western Rhodesia
description: Barotziland-North-Western Rhodesia was a British protectorate established across the upper Zambezi river basin in south-central Africa. Administered by the British South Africa Company under royal charter, the territory recognised the traditional authority of King Lewanika of the Lozi people over internal customary matters through the Lochner Concession. Governed successively from Kalomo and Livingstone, the protectorate oversaw expanding copper exploration before amalgamating with North-Eastern Rhodesia in August 1911 to form the unified protectorate of Northern Rhodesia. \n\n Status: Protectorate administered under chartered company rule; Capital: Kalomo (1899 to 1907) and Livingstone (1907 to 1911); Official languages: English; Common languages: Lozi, Tonga and English; Religion: Traditional beliefs and Protestant Christianity; Government: Chartered company protectorate; Historical era: New Imperialism; Established: 28 November 1899; Disestablished: 17 August 1911; Succeeded by: Northern Rhodesia

name: Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria
description: The Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria was a British administrative territory formed in 1900 through the amalgamation of the Niger Coast Protectorate with the chartered territories of the Royal Niger Company along the lower Niger. Enlarged in 1906 through the incorporation of the Lagos Colony, the territory was directed from the bustling Atlantic port of Lagos by colonial governors including Frederick Lugard. The administration reorganised judicial systems and developed extensive export agriculture until merging with the north in January 1914. \n\n Status: Colony and protectorate of Great Britain; Capital: Lagos; Official languages: English; Common languages: Yoruba, Igbo, Edo and Ijaw; Religion: Christianity, traditional religions and Sunni Islam; Government: Colonial governorship; Historical era: New Imperialism; Established: 1900; Disestablished: 1914; Succeeded by: Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria

name: Mamprusi Kingdom
description: The Mamprusi Kingdom under German protection marks a transitional diplomatic phase during the European partition of the Volta River basin in modern northern Ghana and Togo. Centred around the sacred royal town of Nalerigu, the kingdom briefly concluded treaties acknowledging German imperial oversight to counter encroaching French and British expeditions. The German claim lapsed by 1902 following bilateral diplomatic boundary commissions between Great Britain and Imperial Germany, which integrated the Mamprusi realm into the British Northern Territories of the Gold Coast. \n\n Status: Protectorate of the German Empire; Capital: Nalerigu; Common languages: Mampruli and German; Religion: Traditional African religion and Sunni Islam; Government: Traditional monarchy under colonial protectorate; Historical era: Scramble for Africa; Established: 1900; Disestablished: 1902; Succeeded by: Northern Territories of the Gold Coast

name: Protectorate of Northern Rhodesia
description: The Protectorate of Northern Rhodesia was a British colonial possession spanning the savannas and mineral-rich plateaus of central Africa, covering the territory of modern Zambia. Governed initially from Livingstone by the British South Africa Company under royal charter, the territory passed to direct British Colonial Office administration in 1924, subsequent to which the capital shifted inland to Lusaka. The colony underwent massive industrialisation following the discovery of the Copperbelt deposits before achieving sovereign independence as the Republic of Zambia in October 1964. \n\n Status: Protectorate of Great Britain; Capital: Livingstone (until 1935) and Lusaka (from 1935); Official languages: English; Common languages: Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga and Lozi; Religion: Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Colonial governorship; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 29 January 1900; Disestablished: 24 October 1964; Succeeded by: Republic of Zambia

name: American Samoa
description: American Samoa is an unincorporated and unorganised insular territory of the United States encompassing the eastern islands of the Samoan archipelago in the South Pacific Ocean. Acquired through local cessions of sovereignty confirmed after the 1899 Tripartite Convention between Britain, Germany and the United States, the territory was placed under United States Navy administration centred at the deep-water harbour of Pago Pago. In the mid-twentieth century, governance was transferred to civilian authorities under the United States Department of the Interior while preserving indigenous communal land customs. \n\n Status: Unincorporated territory of the United States; Capital: Pago Pago; Official languages: Samoan and English; Common languages: Samoan and English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Devolved constitutional dependency; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 16 February 1900; Preceded by: Kingdom of Samoa

name: German Samoa
description: German Samoa was an Imperial German colonial protectorate encompassing the western Samoan islands of Upolu, Savaiʻi, Manono and Apolima in the South Pacific Ocean. Formalised in February 1900 pursuant to the Tripartite Convention with Great Britain and the United States, the colony was administered from Apia by Governor Wilhelm Solf, who cultivated close ties with traditional Samoan chiefs while promoting copra plantations. German colonial authority ended abruptly in August 1914 when an expeditionary force from New Zealand occupied Apia without resistance at the outbreak of World War I. \n\n Status: Protectorate of the German Empire; Capital: Apia; Official languages: German; Common languages: Samoan and German; Religion: Christianity; Government: Imperial colonial governorship; Historical era: New Imperialism; Established: 16 February 1900; Disestablished: 29 August 1914; Succeeded by: New Zealand Military Administration of Samoa

name: Colony of Chad
description: The Colony of Chad was an expansive French colonial domain established across the Sahelian and Saharan zones of central Africa, extending from the Chari River to the Tibesti Mountains. Instituted following the French defeat of the warlord Rabih az-Zubayr at Kousséri in April 1900, the possession was administered from Fort-Lamy and incorporated into the federation of French Equatorial Africa. Under Governor Félix Éboué in 1940, the colony distinguished itself as the first French overseas territory to declare loyalty to Charles de Gaulle's Free French forces before achieving independence in August 1960. \n\n Status: Colony of France; Capital: N'Djamena; Official languages: French; Common languages: Chadian Arabic, Sara, Kanembu and French; Religion: Sunni Islam, Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Colonial governorship; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 22 April 1900; Disestablished: 11 August 1960; Succeeded by: Republic of Chad

name: Orange River Colony
description: The Orange River Colony was a British Crown colony established in southern Africa following the military occupation and formal annexation of the Boer Orange Free State during the Second Boer War. Governed from Bloemfontein by a British colonial governor, the administration supervised reconstruction efforts, repatriation of Boer families and development of modern infrastructure across the highveld. Granted responsible self-government in 1907, the colony ceased to exist in May 1910 upon joining the Cape, Natal and the Transvaal to form the unified Union of South Africa. \n\n Status: Crown colony of Great Britain; Capital: Bloemfontein; Official languages: English and Dutch; Common languages: Afrikaans, English, Dutch and Sesotho; Religion: Dutch Reformed Church and Anglicanism; Government: Constitutional colonial governorship; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 28 May 1900; Disestablished: 31 May 1910; Succeeded by: Union of South Africa

name: Eight-Nation Alliance
description: The Eight-Nation Alliance was a multinational military coalition formed in the summer of 1900 by Great Britain, France, Germany, Japan, Russia, the United States, Italy and Austria-Hungary. Organised to relieve besieged foreign legations in Beijing during the Boxer Rebellion, the coalition deployed an expeditionary force of forty-five thousand soldiers to defeat imperial Qing armies and insurgent militias. The allied command captured Tianjin and Beijing, subjecting northern China to extensive military occupation and punitive requisitions until the signing of the Boxer Protocol in September 1901. \n\n Status: Multinational military expeditionary coalition; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: English, French, German, Japanese and Russian; Government: Joint Allied military command; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 10 June 1900; Disestablished: 7 September 1901; Succeeded by: Qing Dynasty

name: Beijing Legation Quarter
label: concessions in china
description: The Beijing Legation Quarter was a fortified diplomatic sanctuary situated in the heart of Beijing, immediately east of Tiananmen Square. Formally established as an autonomous enclave under the provisions of the 1901 Boxer Protocol following the fifty-five-day siege of foreign legations, the district was placed outside Chinese municipal jurisdiction and defended by permanent foreign garrisons. Foreign ministers and municipal boards governed the quarter with full extraterritorial legal immunity until the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War led to Japanese occupation in August 1937. \n\n Status: Extraterritorial diplomatic enclave; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: English, French, German, Russian and Mandarin Chinese; Government: Diplomatic municipal council; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 14 August 1900; Disestablished: 8 August 1937; Succeeded by: Republic of China

name: Russian Concession in Tianjin
label: concessions in china
description: The Russian Concession in Tianjin was an extraterritorial commercial district situated on the eastern bank of the Hai River in the northern Chinese treaty port of Tianjin. Acquired by the Russian Empire in December 1900 following the military suppression of the Boxer Rebellion, the concession formed the second-largest foreign enclave in the city, supporting riverine wharves, trade warehouses and residential quarters. Russian consular authorities directed municipal administration until the mid-1920s, after which the territory was formally retroceded to the Chinese Beiyang government. \n\n Status: Treaty port concession of the Russian Empire; Administrative seat: Russian consular municipal office; Common languages: Russian and Mandarin Chinese; Government: Consular municipal administration; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 31 December 1900; Disestablished: 1 July 1927; Succeeded by: Republic of China

name: Commonwealth of Australia
label: british colonies in australia
description: The Commonwealth of Australia was inaugurated on 1 January 1901 as a self-governing federal dominion of the British Empire, uniting the six separate colonies of New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania. Governed under a federal parliamentary constitution that balanced Westminster responsible government with American federalism, the dominion initially operated from Melbourne before transferring its legislature to the planned national capital of Canberra in 1927. Australia exercised expanding domestic autonomy and external sovereignty until formally confirming legislative equality under the Statute of Westminster in December 1931. \n\n Status: Self-governing dominion of the British Empire; Capital: Melbourne (1901 to 1927) and Canberra (from 1927); Official languages: English; Common languages: English and Australian Aboriginal languages; Religion: Christianity; Government: Federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 1901; Disestablished: 11 December 1931; Succeeded by: Australia

name: Jhabua State
label: indian princely states
description: Jhabua State was an ancient Rajput princely domain situated in the hilly tracts of the Malwa plateau within the Central India Agency of the British Raj. Governed by a Rathore dynasty from the capital of Jhabua, the state contained a predominantly indigenous Bhil and Bhilala population engaged in subsistence farming and forest cultivation. The ruling prince administered domestic civil and criminal justice under the guidance of British political agents until signing the instrument of accession to the Dominion of India in 1948. \n\n Status: Princely state under British suzerainty; Capital: Jhabua; Common languages: Bhili, Malvi and Hindi; Religion: Hinduism and animism; Government: Hereditary monarchy; Historical era: British Raj; Established: 1901; Disestablished: 1948; Succeeded by: India

name: Sheikhdom of Shaib
label: southern arabia petty kingdoms
description: The Sheikhdom of Shaib was a mountainous Arab tribal principality situated in the rugged highlands of the Western Aden Protectorate in southern Arabia. Governed by hereditary sheikhs of the Saqladi lineage from the mountain fortress town of Awbil, the sheikhdom retained traditional tribal autonomy while entering into formal protectorate relations with Great Britain at the start of the twentieth century. The state maintained its distinct customary governance until February 1959, when it amalgamated into the British-sponsored Federation of Arab Emirates of the South. \n\n Status: Protectorate of Great Britain; Capital: Awbil; Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Hereditary sheikhdom; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 1901; Disestablished: 11 February 1959; Succeeded by: Federation of Arab Emirates of the South

name: Sheikhdom of Kuwait (Military Occupation)
description: The Sheikhdom of Kuwait under military occupation designates the forward operational campaign conducted by Sheikh Mubarak Al-Sabah into central Nejd in early 1901. Mobilising a coalition of eastern Arabian tribes alongside exiled Saudi warriors, Sheikh Mubarak launched an offensive deep into the Arabian interior to challenge the regional supremacy of the Rashidi Emirate of Jabal Shammar. Kuwaiti forces briefly established martial control over disputed desert pastures before suffering a decisive tactical defeat at the Battle of Sarif in March 1901, forcing an immediate retreat to Kuwait. \n\n Status: Military occupation zone under Kuwaiti command; Administrative seat: Mobile tribal military camp; Common languages: Najdi Arabic and Kuwaiti Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Sheikhly military command; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 25 February 1901; Disestablished: 31 March 1901; Succeeded by: Emirate of Jabal Shammar

name: Dir State
label: indian princely states
description: Dir State was an autonomous Pashtun princely principality situated in the rugged Hindu Raj mountains of the North-West Frontier Province of British India. Governed by hereditary khans of the Akhundkhel clan from the fortified town of Dir, the state occupied a crucial strategic position controlling the Lowari Pass between Malakand and Chitral. Under a subsidiary alliance with the British Raj established in 1902, the ruler enjoyed internal sovereignty and tribal jurisdiction until the realm formally acceded to the Dominion of Pakistan in August 1948. \n\n Status: Princely state under British suzerainty; Capital: Dir; Common languages: Pashto; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Traditional absolute principality; Historical era: British Raj; Established: 1902; Disestablished: 2 August 1948; Succeeded by: Pakistan

name: Emirate of Riyadh
description: The Emirate of Riyadh was the foundational phase of the third Saudi state, established on 13 January 1902 when Abdulaziz Al Saud, known as Ibn Saud, stormed the Masmak fortress in Riyadh. Having captured the ancestral city from Rashidi governors, Ibn Saud proclaimed himself ruler of Nejd and commenced the systematic consolidation of central Arabian oasis towns and bedouin tribes. Supported by the religious zeal of the emerging Ikhwan brotherhood, the emirate expanded continuously across the central desert until capturing the coastal oasis of Al-Hasa from the Ottomans in May 1913. \n\n Status: Sovereign absolute monarchy; Capital: Riyadh; Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Najdi Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Islamic absolute monarchy; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 13 January 1902; Disestablished: 1 May 1913; Preceded by: Emirate of Jabal Shammar; Succeeded by: Emirate of Nejd and Hasa

name: Territory of Papua
description: The Territory of Papua was an external dependency of the Commonwealth of Australia encompassing the south-eastern quadrant of the island of New Guinea and adjacent maritime archipelagos. Formally transferred from British imperial administration to Australian federal oversight in 1902 and regularised under the Papua Act of 1905, the territory was administered from Port Moresby by Lieutenant-Governor Sir Hubert Murray. The colonial regime promoted plantation agriculture and mining while enforcing protective paternalistic indigenous policies until World War II necessitated joint civil-military administration. \n\n Status: External territory of Australia; Capital: Port Moresby; Official languages: English; Common languages: Hiri Motu, Tok Pisin and Papuan languages; Religion: Traditional religions and Christianity; Government: Colonial lieutenant-governorship; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 18 March 1902; Disestablished: 6 September 1945; Succeeded by: Territory of Papua and New Guinea

name: Guantanamo Bay Naval Base
description: Guantanamo Bay Naval Base is an extraterritorial military installation and naval facility of the United States situated on forty-five square miles along Guantánamo Bay in south-eastern Cuba. Secured under an open-ended lease treaty signed in February 1903 following the conclusion of the Spanish-American War, the base served as a vital coaling depot and fleet station protecting Caribbean shipping approaches to the Panama Canal. While successive Cuban revolutionary governments have protested the American military presence as an infringement of national sovereignty, the installation remains continuously maintained under permanent federal command. \n\n Status: Extraterritorial military base of the United States; Administrative seat: Guantanamo Bay; Common languages: English and Spanish; Government: Naval military station; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 20 May 1902; Preceded by: United States Military Government in Cuba

name: Kulangsu International Settlement
label: concessions in china
description: The Kulangsu International Settlement was a multilateral foreign enclave established on Gulangyu Island directly facing the treaty port of Xiamen in Fujian province, China. Formalised on 1 June 1902 through Land Regulations agreed between the Qing imperial government and foreign consular representatives, the island was administered by an elected international municipal council dominated by British and Western commercial interests. The settlement developed into a picturesque residential and diplomatic haven with Western consulates, churches and private mansions, continuing its autonomous administration until wartime Japanese occupation in 1943. \n\n Status: Multilateral treaty port settlement; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: English, Hokkien and Mandarin Chinese; Government: International municipal council; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 1 June 1902; Disestablished: 1943; Succeeded by: Republic of China

name: Italian Concession in Tianjin
label: concessions in china
description: The Italian Concession in Tianjin was an extraterritorial urban district granted to the Kingdom of Italy on 7 June 1902 following the Boxer Protocol in northern China. Positioned on the eastern bank of the Hai River between the Austro-Hungarian and Russian concessions, the enclave was developed into a gracious European quarter featuring Mediterranean architecture, tree-lined boulevards and consular residences. Administered by an Italian royal consul and an advisory municipal board, the concession retained its extraterritorial status until Italian forces surrendered control to the Japanese army in September 1943. \n\n Status: Treaty port concession of the Kingdom of Italy; Administrative seat: Italian consular municipal office; Common languages: Italian and Mandarin Chinese; Government: Consular municipal administration; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 7 June 1902; Disestablished: 10 September 1943; Succeeded by: Republic of China

name: Insular Government of the Philippine Islands
description: The Insular Government of the Philippine Islands was an organised unincorporated territory of the United States established across the Philippine archipelago under the Philippine Organic Act of July 1902. Successor to American military rule, the administration was headed by a federally appointed civil Governor-General in Manila and featured a bicameral legislature comprising the Philippine Commission and an elected Philippine Assembly. The insular regime oversaw public education, infrastructure construction and progressive devolution of executive power until transitioning into the semi-autonomous Commonwealth of the Philippines in February 1935. \n\n Status: Organised unincorporated territory of the United States; Capital: Manila; Official languages: English and Spanish; Common languages: Tagalog, Ilocano, Cebuano and Hokkien; Religion: Roman Catholicism, traditional religions and Sunni Islam; Government: Devolved presidential dependency; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 1 July 1902; Disestablished: 8 February 1935; Succeeded by: Commonwealth of the Philippines

name: Dervish State
description: The Dervish State was an anti-colonial Islamic theocratic realm founded in the Somali interior by the religious leader and poet Sayyid Mohammed Abdullah Hassan. Operating from the fortified capital of Taleh in the Nugaal valley, the Dervish forces mobilised tens of thousands of warriors across clan divisions to resist British, Italian and Ethiopian imperial encroachment. The state constructed stone citadels, established regular cavalry regiments and maintained sovereign defiance for two decades until British air and ground operations decisively destroyed its fortifications in December 1920. \n\n Status: Sovereign Islamic theocracy; Capital: Taleh; Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Somali and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Theocratic executive council; Historical era: New Imperialism; Established: 1 September 1902; Disestablished: 21 December 1920; Succeeded by: British Somaliland and Italian Somaliland

name: Belgian Concession in Tianjin
label: concessions in china
description: The Belgian Concession in Tianjin was an extraterritorial commercial district acquired by the Kingdom of Belgium along the eastern bank of the Hai River in northern China. Established on 1 December 1902 through negotiations led by diplomat Maurice Joostens in the wake of the Boxer Rebellion, the concession was envisioned as an industrial and warehousing base for Belgian manufacturing and railway syndicates. Due to modest investment and low commercial traffic, the Belgian government concluded that maintaining municipal oversight was uneconomic, formally retroceding the parcel to the Republic of China in January 1931. \n\n Status: Treaty port concession of the Kingdom of Belgium; Administrative seat: Belgian consular municipal office; Common languages: French, Dutch and Mandarin Chinese; Government: Consular municipal administration; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 1 December 1902; Disestablished: 15 January 1931; Succeeded by: Republic of China

name: Austro-Hungarian Concession in Tianjin
label: concessions in china
description: The Austro-Hungarian Concession in Tianjin was an extraterritorial riverfront enclave granted to the Dual Monarchy of Austria-Hungary on 27 December 1902 under the Boxer Protocol. Located along the Hai River north-east of the Italian concession, the enclave contained modern residential streets, a consular building, a hospital and commercial bathhouses. Governed by Austro-Hungarian consular authorities and an elected council, the concession was the shortest-lived foreign enclave in Tianjin, terminating on 14 August 1917 when China declared war on the Central Powers and seized the territory. \n\n Status: Treaty port concession of Austria-Hungary; Administrative seat: Austro-Hungarian consular office; Common languages: German, Hungarian and Mandarin Chinese; Government: Consular municipal administration; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 27 December 1902; Disestablished: 14 August 1917; Succeeded by: Republic of China

name: Gurian Republic
description: The Gurian Republic was an insurgent peasant democracy and socialist commune that flourished between 1903 and 1907 in the western Georgian region of Guria within the Russian Empire. Sparked by peasant resistance against excessive land rents and Tsarist taxation, the community expelled imperial bureaucrats and police, instituting democratic village assemblies and elected popular courts centred at Ozurgeti. The republic maintained collective administration and armed self-defence until the Tsarist regime deployed overwhelming Cossack military columns in 1906 and 1907 to brutally crush the uprising and restore imperial rule. \n\n Status: Autonomous peasant revolutionary republic; Capital: Ozurgeti; Common languages: Georgian; Religion: Georgian Orthodoxy; Government: Direct democratic assembly; Historical era: Russian Revolution of 1905; Established: 1903; Disestablished: 1907; Succeeded by: Russian Empire

name: Igbirra
description: Igbirra, modernly identified as the Ebira Kingdom, was an indigenous central Nigerian realm situated in the hilly territory south-west of the Niger and Benue confluence. Governed from the principal political seat of Okene by traditional clan chiefs and priest-rulers, the polity defended its independence against Fulani jihadist incursions and preserved ancestral metallurgy, textile manufacturing and agricultural traditions. Between 1903 and 1904, expeditionary columns of the British West African Frontier Force subjugated local hill fortifications, bringing the sovereign kingdom under the indirect rule of the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria. \n\n Status: Traditional kingdom; Capital: Okene; Common languages: Ebira; Religion: Traditional African religion and Sunni Islam; Government: Traditional chieftaincy; Historical era: Scramble for Africa; Established: 1903; Disestablished: 1904; Succeeded by: Protectorate of Northern Nigeria

name: Independent State of Acre
description: The Independent State of Acre between 24 and 27 January 1903 represents the culminating revolutionary phase of the Acre War, when Brazilian rubber insurrections seized the territory from Bolivian authorities. Led by commander José Plácido de Castro, the insurgents captured the fortified Bolivian garrison at Puerto Alonso, immediately declaring Acre an independent sovereign republic. This brief proclamation established effective Brazilian revolutionary control on the ground, setting the diplomatic foundation for the Treaty of Petrópolis later that year, which permanently incorporated the territory into Brazil. \n\n Status: Revolutionary secessionist republic; Capital: None (decentralised); Official languages: Portuguese; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Revolutionary military council; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 24 January 1903; Disestablished: 27 January 1903; Preceded by: Republic of Bolivia; Succeeded by: Independent State of Acre (consolidated)

name: Colony of Mauritania
description: The Colony of Mauritania was a French colonial domain established across the arid western Sahara and the northern valley of the Senegal River. Initiated in May 1903 through the pacification campaigns and protectorate treaties negotiated by Xavier Coppolani with traditional Moorish emirs, the territory was initially administered from Saint-Louis in Senegal as part of French West Africa. Overcoming stubborn desert resistance in the Adrar highlands, French authorities oversaw pastoral nomadism and coastal fisheries until Mauritania transferred its administrative capital to Nouakchott and achieved independence in November 1960. \n\n Status: Colony of France; Capital: Saint-Louis (until 1957) and Nouakchott (from 1957); Official languages: French; Common languages: Hassaniya Arabic, Pulaar, Soninke and Wolof; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Colonial governorship; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 21 May 1903; Disestablished: 28 November 1960; Succeeded by: Islamic Republic of Mauritania

name: Republic of Kruševo
description: The Republic of Kruševo was an unrecognised revolutionary state proclaimed on 3 August 1903 during the anti-Ottoman Ilinden-Preobrazhenie Uprising in Ottoman Macedonia. Organised by insurgents of the Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organisation under the presidency of schoolteacher Nikola Karev, the republican leadership seized the mountain town of Kruševo and promulgated the historic Kruševo Manifesto appealing for inter-ethnic brotherhood. After ten days of democratic governance, overwhelming Ottoman imperial troops besieged and bombarded the town, extinguishing the short-lived republic on 13 August 1903. \n\n Status: Revolutionary provisional republic; Capital: Kruševo; Common languages: Macedonian, Bulgarian and Aromanian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Revolutionary provisional council; Historical era: Ilinden Uprising; Established: 3 August 1903; Disestablished: 13 August 1903; Preceded by: Ottoman Empire; Succeeded by: Ottoman Empire

name: Strandzha Republic
description: The Strandzha Republic, also celebrated as the Strandzha Commune, was a libertarian socialist commune proclaimed on 18 August 1903 in the Strandzha Mountains of Eastern Thrace during the Preobrazhenie Uprising. Led by Bulgarian anarchist revolutionary Mihail Gerdzhikov of the Internal Macedonian Adrianople Revolutionary Organisation, the insurgents liberated Malko Tarnovo and established an egalitarian communal order that distributed food, abolished tax registers and ended Ottoman authority. The revolutionary experiment endured for three weeks before superior Ottoman military forces invaded the highlands in September 1903, burning rebel villages and restoring imperial control. \n\n Status: Anarchist revolutionary commune; Capital: Malko Tarnovo; Common languages: Bulgarian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy and secularism; Government: Revolutionary committee; Historical era: Preobrazhenie Uprising; Established: 18 August 1903; Disestablished: 8 September 1903; Preceded by: Ottoman Empire; Succeeded by: Ottoman Empire

name: Republic of Panama
description: The Republic of Panama is a sovereign Central American nation spanning the narrow isthmus between the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean. Formalising its separation from Colombia on 3 November 1903 with naval and diplomatic backing from the United States, the newly proclaimed republic granted America concessionary rights to finish and operate the strategic interoceanic Panama Canal. Governed from Panama City, the state weathered recurring political crises and foreign interventions before assuming uninhibited national control over the canal and its surrounding territory at the close of 1999. \n\n Status: Sovereign presidential republic; Capital: Panama City; Official languages: Spanish; Common languages: Spanish and English; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 3 November 1903; Preceded by: Republic of Colombia

name: Panama Canal Zone
description: The Panama Canal Zone was an unincorporated concessionary territory of the United States encompassing a five-mile-wide strip on either side of the Panama Canal across the Isthmus of Panama. Established under the controversial Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty of November 1903 and operational from 1904, the zone was administered from Balboa by federally appointed military and civilian governors. Functioning as a self-contained American enclave with separate schools, courts and postal services, the territory was disestablished in 1979 under the Torrijos-Carter Treaties, returning completely to Panamanian sovereignty. \n\n Status: Concessionary territory of the United States; Capital: Balboa; Common languages: English and Spanish; Government: Territorial civil and military administration; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 1904; Disestablished: 1980; Succeeded by: Republic of Panama

name: Free State of Counani
description: The Free State of Counani was an unrecognised secessionist entity proclaimed in the disputed Amazonian borderland between French Guiana and the Brazilian state of Amapá. Revived in 1905 by the French adventurer Adolphe Brézet, who styled himself Duke of Brezet and claimed to lead a council of native and Afro-descended rubber tappers from the settlement of Counani, the entity sought foreign financial loans and issued philatelic stamps. Ignored by both Brazilian and French authorities following international arbitration that recognised Brazilian sovereignty over the region, the phantom state dissolved by 1913. \n\n Status: Unrecognised self-proclaimed state; Capital: Counani; Official languages: French; Common languages: French, Portuguese and Guyanese Creole; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Self-proclaimed authoritarian republic; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 1905; Disestablished: 1913; Succeeded by: First Brazilian Republic

name: Imamate of Yemen
description: The Imamate of Yemen during the early twentieth century designates the autonomous Zaidi state revived in the northern highlands by Imam Yahya Muhammad Hamid ed-Din. In 1905, Yahya rallied mountain tribes in a widespread rebellion against Ottoman imperial garrisons, expelling Ottoman forces from Sana'a and establishing his royal court at the mountain stronghold of Shaharah. The imamate maintained defiant domestic administration and traditional Islamic law in the highlands until October 1911, when the Treaty of Daan formally recognised the Imam's autonomous judicial authority within the Ottoman Empire. \n\n Status: Autonomous Zaidi imamate; Capital: Shaharah; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Zaidi Shia Islam; Government: Theocratic hereditary imamate; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 1905; Disestablished: 9 October 1911; Succeeded by: Yemen Vilayet

name: Dervish State
description: The Dervish State under the 1905 Italian accord refers to the recognised territorial enclave conceded to Sayyid Mohammed Abdullah Hassan along the northern Somali coastline and Nugaal valley. Under the Illig Agreement signed in March 1905, Italian colonial authorities granted the Dervish leader autonomous jurisdiction over the territory between the Sultanate of Hobyo and the Majeerteen Sultanate in exchange for peace. The arrangement provided temporary regional stability until 1912, when renewed hostilities between Dervish forces and British and Italian garrisons shattered the pact. \n\n Status: Autonomous theocratic territory under treaty accord; Capital: Taleh; Common languages: Somali and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Theocratic khusuusi council; Historical era: New Imperialism; Established: 3 March 1905; Disestablished: 1912; Succeeded by: Dervish State (resumed insurgency)

name: Kwantung Leased Territory
label: concessions in china
description: The Kwantung Leased Territory was an Imperial Japanese leased concession occupying the southern tip of the Liaodong Peninsula in north-eastern China. Acquired from the Russian Empire in September 1905 under the Treaty of Portsmouth following the Russo-Japanese War, the territory encompassed the strategic naval bastion of Port Arthur and the flourishing commercial port of Dairen. Administered by a Japanese governor-general in coordination with the Kwantung Army and the South Manchuria Railway Company, the concession served as Japan's continental springboard until Soviet forces liberated the peninsula in August 1945. \n\n Status: Leased territory of the Empire of Japan; Capital: Dalian; Official languages: Japanese; Common languages: Japanese and Mandarin Chinese; Government: Colonial governorship; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 5 September 1905; Disestablished: 14 August 1945; Succeeded by: Soviet Military Administration of Kwantung

name: Korean Empire
description: The Korean Empire under Japanese protectorate designates the final years of the Daehan state following the coerced signing of the Eulsa Treaty on 17 November 1905. Stripped of diplomatic independence, the realm was subordinated to the newly created office of the Japanese Resident-General in Hanseong, who exercised sweeping supervisory powers over internal administration, finance and foreign affairs. After Emperor Gojong was forced to abdicate in 1907 following his secret appeal to the Second Hague Peace Conference, Japan formally annexed the peninsula on 29 August 1910, terminating the empire. \n\n Status: Protectorate of the Empire of Japan; Capital: Hanseong; Official languages: Korean; Religion: Neo-Confucianism, Buddhism and Christianity; Government: Absolute monarchy under colonial protectorate; Historical era: Century of humiliation; Established: 17 November 1905; Disestablished: 29 August 1910; Succeeded by: Japanese Korea

name: Colony of Ubangi-Shari-Chad
description: The Colony of Ubangi-Shari-Chad was an administrative amalgamation created by French colonial authorities in central Africa on 11 February 1906. Uniting the civilian territory of Ubangi-Shari with the Military Territory of Chad, the vast dependency was governed from Fort-de-Possel before Bangui became the primary regional administrative hub. The administrative merger aimed to streamline military supply lines and tax collection across the savanna basin until April 1916, when French authorities partitioned the territory into two separate colonial lieutenant-governorships within French Equatorial Africa. \n\n Status: Colony of France; Capital: Fort-de-Possel; Official languages: French; Common languages: Sango, Chadian Arabic, Sara and Banda; Religion: Sunni Islam, Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Colonial lieutenant-governorship; Historical era: New Imperialism; Established: 11 February 1906; Disestablished: 12 April 1916; Succeeded by: Ubangi-Shari and French Chad

name: Protectorate of Swaziland
description: The Protectorate of Swaziland was a British colonial dependency in southern Africa encompassing the traditional homeland of the Swazi people, bordered on three sides by South Africa and on the east by Mozambique. Placed under direct British administration as a High Commission Territory on 31 March 1906 following the Second Boer War, the territory was directed from Mbabane by a British resident commissioner. Traditional monarchical institutions endured under the long reign of King Sobhuza II, who guided the nation to full sovereign independence as the Kingdom of Swaziland on 6 September 1968. \n\n Status: Protectorate of Great Britain; Capital: Mbabane; Official languages: English and Swazi; Common languages: Swazi and English; Religion: Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Traditional monarchy under colonial protectorate; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 31 March 1906; Disestablished: 6 September 1968; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Swaziland

name: Idrisid Emirate of Asir
description: The Idrisid Emirate of Asir was an autonomous Arab realm established in 1907 along the Red Sea coastal plain of Tihamah in south-western Arabia. Founded by Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi, head of the Idrisiyya Sufi order who rebelled against Ottoman imperial authority, the emirate was governed from the inland oasis city of Sabya. Allied with Great Britain during the First World War, the state expanded its influence over neighbouring ports before increasing pressure from the Wahhabi movement led to an agreement placing the emirate under Saudi protection in October 1926. \n\n Status: Sovereign Islamic emirate; Capital: Sabya; Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Theocratic hereditary emirate; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 1907; Disestablished: 21 October 1926; Succeeded by: Idrisid Emirate of Asir (Saudi protectorate)

name: New Hebrides Condominium
description: The New Hebrides Condominium was an Anglo-French colonial condominium established in 1907 across the Melanesian archipelago now known as Vanuatu. Governed jointly by British and French resident commissioners seated in the capital of Port Vila, the territory was characterised by dual administrative structures, separate legal codes, duplicate police forces and distinct educational systems for Anglophone and Francophone communities. This unusual colonial condominium persisted through the Second World War until rising indigenous nationalism culminated in the declaration of sovereign independence as the Republic of Vanuatu on 30 July 1980. \n\n Status: Condominium of Great Britain and France; Capital: Port Vila; Official languages: English, French and Bislama; Common languages: Bislama, French, English and indigenous Melanesian languages; Religion: Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Joint colonial condominium; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 1907; Disestablished: 30 July 1980; Succeeded by: Republic of Vanuatu

name: Nyasaland Protectorate
description: The Nyasaland Protectorate was a British colonial dependency in south-eastern Africa, reconstituted on 6 July 1907 from the former British Central Africa Protectorate. Administered from Zomba along the western shores of Lake Nyasa, the colony developed an export economy based on tea, tobacco and cotton plantations while supplying migrant labour to Southern Rhodesian and South African mines. Popular opposition to European settler domination and the Central African Federation spurred a powerful nationalist movement led by Hastings Banda, leading to independence as Malawi on 6 July 1964. \n\n Status: Protectorate of Great Britain; Capital: Zomba; Official languages: English; Common languages: Chewa, Yao, Tumbuka and English; Religion: Christianity, traditional beliefs and Sunni Islam; Government: Colonial governorship; Historical era: Late Modern; Established: 6 July 1907; Disestablished: 6 July 1964; Succeeded by: Malawi

name: Dominion of New Zealand
description: The Dominion of New Zealand was established on 26 September 1907 following a royal proclamation by King Edward VII that elevated the former self-governing colony within the British Empire. Operating with a bicameral parliament based in Wellington, the new dominion maintained constitutional ties with the British Crown while managing its domestic laws, social programmes and regional commerce. Over the subsequent four decades, the nation gradually expanded its independent foreign policy before formally ratifying the Statute of Westminster in November 1947. \n\n Status: Dominion of the British Empire; Capital and largest city: Wellington; Common languages: English and Māori; Government: Unitary parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Ruler title: King; Legislature: General Assembly; Historical era: Early twentieth century; Currency: New Zealand pound

name: French Protectorate in Morocco
description: The French Protectorate in Morocco was established following military interventions at Casablanca and Oujda, culminating in the formal signature of the Treaty of Fez in March 1912. Under this colonial arrangement, the French resident-general directed public finances, imperial defence and foreign diplomacy while preserving the Alawi sultan as nominal religious and domestic sovereign. Governed from Rabat, the protectorate oversaw extensive infrastructure modernisation alongside persistent armed resistance until Morocco achieved full independence in April 1956. \n\n Status: Protectorate of France; Capital: Rabat; Official languages: French; Common languages: Moroccan Arabic and Berber languages; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Colonial protectorate under absolute monarchy; Ruler title: Sultan; Currency: Moroccan franc

name: Kingdom of Bhutan
description: The Kingdom of Bhutan was established on 17 December 1907 when regional chieftains and Buddhist clergy unanimously crowned Ugyen Wangchuck as the first hereditary Druk Gyalpo. Through the Treaty of Punakha in 1910, the Himalayan monarchy preserved its internal sovereignty while agreeing to British guidance regarding foreign affairs. Governed from Thimphu, the royal administration consolidated authority across mountainous valleys, ensuring domestic stability and laying the groundwork for modern state institutions. \n\n Status: British protectorate; Capital: Thimphu; Official languages: Dzongkha; Religion: Vajrayana Buddhism; Government: Semi-constitutional hereditary monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Wangchuck; Ruler title: Druk Gyalpo; Historical era: Modern era; Currency: Indian rupee

name: Dominion of Newfoundland
description: The Dominion of Newfoundland was a self-governing member of the British Empire encompassing the island of Newfoundland and mainland Labrador. Administered from St. John's, the territory exercised autonomous legislative and fiscal authority through its bicameral General Assembly independently of neighbouring Canada. Acute economic dislocation caused by the First World War and the Great Depression severely undermined public finances, ultimately prompting the voluntary suspension of self-government in 1934. \n\n Status: Dominion of the British Empire; Capital and largest city: St. John's; Official languages: English; Government: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Ruler title: King; Legislature: General Assembly; Historical era: Interwar period; Currency: Newfoundland dollar

name: Kingdom of Bulgaria
description: The Kingdom of Bulgaria was proclaimed on 5 October 1908 when Prince Ferdinand declared full independence from the Ottoman Empire and assumed the historic title of Tsar. Centred upon Sofia, the Balkan monarchy mobilised substantial armies to pursue national unification across Thrace and Macedonia during the Balkan Wars and the First World War. Despite repeated battlefield campaigns, the kingdom suffered major territorial losses before falling under Soviet influence at the close of the Second World War. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital and largest city: Sofia; Official languages: Bulgarian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Saxe-Coburg and Gotha-Koháry; Ruler title: Tsar; Legislature: National Assembly; Currency: Bulgarian lev

name: Belgian Congo
description: The Belgian Congo was created on 15 November 1908 when the Belgian parliament formally annexed the territory, ending the personal domain of King Leopold II over the Congo Free State. Administered from Boma and subsequently Léopoldville, colonial rule functioned through close cooperation between state administrators, Roman Catholic missions and large private concession companies. The colony developed intensive rubber, copper and diamond extraction networks before surging nationalist mobilisation led to Congolese independence in June 1960. \n\n Status: Belgian crown colony; Capital: Léopoldville; Official languages: French; Common languages: Lingala, Kongo, Swahili and Tshiluba; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial administration; Ruler title: King of the Belgians; Currency: Belgian Congo franc

name: Sultanate of Kedah
label: unfederated malay states
description: The Sultanate of Kedah came under British protection in July 1909 following the Anglo-Siamese Treaty, which transferred suzerainty over northern Malay states from Bangkok to Great Britain. Governed as an unfederated Malay state from its royal seat at Alor Setar, the realm preserved its native nobility, Islamic legal traditions and civil administration alongside an appointed British adviser. Kedah maintained its traditional agrarian economy and distinct cultural autonomy until Japanese forces invaded the peninsula in December 1941. \n\n Status: British protectorate; Historical region: Unfederated Malay States; Capital: Alor Setar; Common languages: Kedah Malay and English; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy under colonial protectorate; Ruler title: Sultan; Preceded by: Kingdom of Siam; Currency: Straits dollar

name: Sultanate of Kelantan
label: unfederated malay states
description: The Sultanate of Kelantan became a British protectorate in July 1909 after the Treaty of Bangkok formally relinquished Siamese tributary claims over the territory. Administered as an unfederated Malay state with its royal capital at Kota Bharu, the sultanate retained its traditional Malay aristocratic structure and Islamic jurisprudence while receiving a British adviser to oversee financial policy. Kelantan preserved its peaceful agrarian lifestyle and conservative cultural institutions until Japanese imperial troops landed on its coast in December 1941. \n\n Status: British protectorate; Historical region: Unfederated Malay States; Capital: Kota Bharu; Common languages: Kelantanese Malay and English; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy under colonial protectorate; Ruler title: Sultan; Preceded by: Kingdom of Siam; Currency: Straits dollar

name: Sultanate of Terengganu
label: unfederated malay states
description: The Sultanate of Terengganu was brought into the British imperial sphere in July 1909 under the terms of the Bangkok Treaty negotiated with Siam. Operating from its historic coastal seat at Kuala Terengganu, the realm maintained its status as an unfederated Malay state governed by its hereditary sultan, whose royal council retained control over internal religious and land customs. The sultanate maintained traditional maritime trade and artisanal industries until Japanese forces occupied the area in December 1941. \n\n Status: British protectorate; Historical region: Unfederated Malay States; Capital: Kuala Terengganu; Common languages: Terengganu Malay and English; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy under colonial protectorate; Ruler title: Sultan; Preceded by: Kingdom of Siam; Currency: Straits dollar

name: State of Perlis
label: unfederated malay states
description: The State of Perlis entered the British imperial network as an unfederated Malay state in July 1909, terminating long-standing Siamese tributary oversight. Governed from Kangar with the royal court based at Arau, the small principality maintained its hereditary Raja and native administration while accepting an appointed British adviser on public revenues and legal matters. Perlis maintained its rural agricultural way of life and communal cohesion until Japanese military forces overran northern Malaya in December 1941. \n\n Status: British protectorate; Historical region: Unfederated Malay States; Capital: Kangar; Common languages: Kedah Malay and English; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Hereditary monarchy under colonial protectorate; Ruler title: Raja; Preceded by: Kingdom of Siam; Currency: Straits dollar

name: Cartier Island
description: Cartier Island was an uninhabited coral reef cay in the Timor Sea that came under direct British imperial jurisdiction following formal annexation in 1909. Located on the outer edge of the Sahul Shelf between northwestern Australia and the Indonesian archipelago, the isolated islet served as a seasonal fishing ground for regional sailors harvesting sea cucumbers. Great Britain maintained title over the reef without founding permanent settlements until transferring administrative control to the Commonwealth of Australia in May 1934. \n\n Status: British crown possession; Capital: None (uninhabited); Common languages: English; Government: Directly administered oceanic territory; Ruler title: King; Historical era: Early twentieth century; Established: 1909; Succeeded by: Commonwealth of Australia; Historical region: Timor Sea

name: Union of South Africa
description: The Union of South Africa was established on 31 May 1910 through the unification of four British colonies: Cape Colony, Natal, the Transvaal and the Orange River Colony. Governed as a self-governing dominion under the British Crown, the state distributed administrative authority across Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein while consolidating political control among the white minority. South Africa contributed armed forces to Allied campaigns during the First World War before attaining sovereign legislative equality through the Statute of Westminster in 1931. \n\n Status: Dominion of the British Empire; Administrative seat: Pretoria; Official languages: English and Dutch; Common languages: Afrikaans, Zulu, Xhosa and Sotho; Government: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Ruler title: King; Legislature: Parliament of South Africa; Established: 31 May 1910; Currency: South African pound

name: Kingdom of Montenegro
description: The Kingdom of Montenegro was proclaimed on 28 August 1910 when Prince Nicholas I assumed the title of King in Cetinje, celebrating half a century of his dynastic reign. Centred upon its rugged mountain capital, the small Balkan monarchy fought in the Balkan Wars to expand its territory towards the Adriatic and eastern interior. After enduring bitter conflict and Austro-Hungarian military occupation during the First World War, the state was integrated into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in November 1918. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital: Cetinje; Common languages: Serbian; Religion: Serbian Orthodoxy; Government: Constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Petrović-Njegoš; Ruler title: King; Established: 28 August 1910; Disestablished: 28 November 1918; Currency: Montenegrin perper

name: Portuguese Republic
description: The Portuguese Republic was established on 5 October 1910 after a revolutionary uprising in Lisbon deposed King Manuel II and abolished the constitutional monarchy. Operating under a secular and democratic constitution adopted in 1911, the republican administration separated church and state, modernised education and introduced broad electoral reforms. Persistent political instability, ministerial turnover and financial distress weakened the regime, leading to its overthrow by a military coup d'état in May 1926. \n\n Status: Sovereign republic; Capital and largest city: Lisbon; Official languages: Portuguese; Government: Parliamentary republic; Head of state: President; Legislature: Congress of the Republic; Established: 5 October 1910; Disestablished: 28 May 1926; Currency: Portuguese escudo

name: Great Mongol State
description: The Great Mongol State emerged in December 1911 when Mongol nobles and Buddhist prelates in Outer Mongolia declared independence during the collapse of the Manchu Qing dynasty. Establishing their government at Niislel Khüree, the assembly enthroned the eighth Jebtsundamba Khutuktu as the Bogd Khaan, combining religious and political authority within a restored monarchy. The state defended its regional autonomy against foreign encroachments before reorganising as the socialist Mongolian People's Republic in November 1924. \n\n Status: Sovereign theocratic monarchy; Capital: Niislel Khüree; Official languages: Mongolian; Religion: Tibetan Buddhism; Government: Theocratic absolute monarchy; Ruler title: Bogd Khaan; Established: 1 December 1911; Disestablished: 26 November 1924; Currency: Mongolian dollar

name: Uryankhay Republic
description: The Uryankhay Republic was proclaimed on 1 December 1911 by Tuvan tribal chieftains and Buddhist dignitaries in the upper Yenisey basin amidst the Chinese Xinhai Revolution. Centred upon the settlement of Belotsarsk, the regional assembly renounced Qing imperial suzerainty and sought diplomatic recognition from the newly formed government in Mongolia. Confronted by regional instability and external pressures, the local leaders petitioned the Russian Empire for protection, resulting in the establishment of a Russian protectorate in April 1914. \n\n Status: Unrecognised republic; Capital: Belotsarsk; Common languages: Tuvan, Mongolian and Russian; Religion: Tibetan Buddhism and Tengrism; Government: Provisional republic; Historical era: Early twentieth century; Established: 1 December 1911; Disestablished: 14 April 1914; Succeeded by: Uryankhay Krai

name: Republic of China
description: The Republic of China was officially established in early 1912 following the Xinhai Revolution and the formal abdication of the last Qing emperor, Puyi. Governed from Beijing under the Beiyang administration headed by President Yuan Shikai, the fledgling republic sought to introduce modern constitutional institutions across the former imperial territories. The new political order fractured when Yuan attempted to establish a short-lived imperial regime, and his death in June 1916 ushered in the prolonged Warlord Era. \n\n Status: Sovereign republic; Capital: Beijing; Official languages: Standard Chinese; Government: Constitutional republic; Head of state: President; Preceded by: Qing dynasty; Established: 12 February 1912; Disestablished: 6 June 1916; Currency: Chinese silver yuan

name: Tripolitania and Cyrenaica
description: Tripolitania and Cyrenaica was an initial unified colonial jurisdiction proclaimed by royal decree of the Kingdom of Italy on 23 February 1912 during the Italo-Turkish War. Governed from the coastal port of Tripoli, Italian military authorities claimed sovereignty over former Ottoman vilayets along the North African coast despite continued armed opposition from local Sanusi irregulars. The provisional administration remained in place until October 1912, when Italy partitioned the territory into separate colonies of Italian Cyrenaica and Italian Tripolitania. \n\n Status: Italian crown colony; Capital: Tripoli; Official languages: Italian; Common languages: Libyan Arabic and Berber languages; Religion: Sunni Islam and Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial military administration; Ruler title: King; Established: 23 February 1912; Disestablished: 18 October 1912

name: Sultanate of Morocco
description: The Sultanate of Morocco designated the traditional Alawi royal administration that continued to direct religious and domestic matters after France imposed a colonial protectorate in March 1912. While French military authorities exercised direct control over foreign relations and strategic coastal ports, the Moroccan sultan maintained his palace court at Fez and promulgated imperial decrees. This administrative arrangement continued through the First World War until colonial authorities consolidated civil rule around the capital of Rabat in 1919. \n\n Status: French protectorate; Capital: Fez; Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Moroccan Arabic and Berber languages; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy under colonial protectorate; Ruling dynasty: Alawi; Ruler title: Sultan; Preceded by: Alawi Sultanate

name: Italian Islands of the Aegean
description: The Italian Islands of the Aegean comprised an archipelago of fourteen Aegean islands, commonly known as the Dodecanese, captured from the Ottoman Empire during the Italo-Turkish War of 1912. Based on the island of Rhodes, the possession was administered by an Italian military governor and subsequently organised into a permanent Mediterranean naval outpost. The administration oversaw civil infrastructure, public port works and urban renovation until German armed forces occupied the archipelago in November 1943. \n\n Status: Italian island possession; Capital: Rhodes; Official languages: Italian; Common languages: Greek and Turkish; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism and Sunni Islam; Government: Colonial governorship; Ruler title: King of Italy; Established: 28 April 1912; Currency: Italian lira

name: Ganden Phodrang
description: Ganden Phodrang was the traditional theocratic governing system of Tibet that operated as a de facto independent state after imperial Qing garrisons were expelled from Lhasa in 1912. Guided by the Dalai Lama from the Potala Palace, the administration maintained Buddhist monastic institutions, managed regional diplomacy and maintained a standing army. The state preserved its spiritual autonomy and religious traditions across the Tibetan plateau until the signing of the Seventeen Point Agreement with the People's Republic of China in May 1951. \n\n Status: Sovereign theocratic state; Capital: Lhasa; Common languages: Tibetan; Religion: Tibetan Buddhism; Government: Dual religious and secular theocracy; Head of state: Dalai Lama; Established: 1 August 1912; Disestablished: 23 May 1951; Currency: Tibetan srang

name: Territory of Alaska
description: The Territory of Alaska was established on 24 August 1912 when the United States Congress passed the Second Organic Act, converting the former District of Alaska into an organised incorporated territory. Governed from Juneau with a federally appointed governor and an elected territorial legislature, the subarctic region experienced rapid commercial growth in fisheries, mining and forestry. The territory served as a strategic theatre during the Second World War before being granted full American statehood in January 1959. \n\n Status: Organised incorporated territory of the United States; Capital: Juneau; Official languages: English; Common languages: English and Alaska Native languages; Government: Territorial democracy; Ruler title: Governor; Legislature: Alaska Territorial Legislature; Established: 24 August 1912; Disestablished: 3 January 1959; Currency: United States dollar

name: Italian Cyrenaica
description: Italian Cyrenaica was a colonial territory in eastern Libya established after the Ottoman Empire relinquished the region to Italy under the 1912 Treaty of Ouchy. Governed from the coastal city of Benghazi, Italian authorities confronted extensive and sustained guerrilla resistance from the indigenous Sanusi brotherhood across the interior plateaus. Italian military commanders conducted an intense pacification campaign in the late 1920s before integrating the territory into unified Italian Libya in 1934. \n\n Status: Italian crown colony; Capital: Benghazi; Official languages: Italian; Common languages: Libyan Arabic and Berber languages; Religion: Sunni Islam and Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial governorship; Ruler title: King of Italy; Established: 18 October 1912; Disestablished: 1 January 1934; Currency: Italian lira

name: Italian Tripolitania
description: Italian Tripolitania was an Italian colonial possession in western Libya established following the conclusion of the Italo-Turkish War in October 1912. Administered from the historic seaport of Tripoli, the colonial regime invested in transport networks, agricultural colonisation and public utilities while facing frequent insurgent movements from local Arab and Berber tribes. Italian authority retreated to coastal enclaves during the First World War before being re-established and merged into a single Libyan colony in 1934. \n\n Status: Italian crown colony; Capital: Tripoli; Official languages: Italian; Common languages: Libyan Arabic and Berber languages; Religion: Sunni Islam and Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial governorship; Ruler title: King of Italy; Established: 18 October 1912; Disestablished: 1 January 1934; Currency: Italian lira

name: Southern Military Territory
description: The Southern Military Territory was an administrative jurisdiction established by the Kingdom of Italy to oversee the vast Saharan desert interior of the Fezzan. Centred upon the oasis settlement of Murzuk, the territory remained under martial administration headed by military officers tasked with patrolling trade tracks and securing remote water holes. Italian garrisons were repeatedly forced to withdraw by regional insurgent forces before firmly establishing control and incorporating the district into Italian Libya in 1934. \n\n Status: Military occupation zone; Administrative seat: Murzuk; Official languages: Italian; Common languages: Libyan Arabic, Tuareg and Toubou; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military administration; Ruler title: King of Italy; Established: 18 October 1912; Disestablished: 1 January 1934

name: Kingdom of Serbia and Kingdom of Montenegro (Military Occupation)
description: The Kingdom of Serbia and Kingdom of Montenegro (Military Occupation) was a joint martial administration established across northern Albania during the First Balkan War. Allied Serbian and Montenegrin forces advanced into Ottoman territories in late 1912, occupying coastal ports and strategic highland towns to secure maritime access to the Adriatic Sea. Under intense diplomatic pressure from the European Great Powers and the terms of the Treaty of London, both kingdoms evacuated their troops in May 1913 to respect Albanian independence. \n\n Status: Joint military occupation zone; Capital: None (decentralised); Common languages: Serbian and Albanian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism and Sunni Islam; Government: Joint military administration; Historical era: First Balkan War; Established: 4 November 1912; Disestablished: 30 May 1913

name: Spanish Protectorate in Morocco
description: The Spanish Protectorate in Morocco was established on 27 November 1912 following a bilateral convention with France that granted Spain administrative authority over northern Morocco and the Cape Juby strip. Governed from Tétouan by a Spanish high commissioner alongside a representative of the Moroccan sultan, the territory was marked by bitter rural warfare against Berber tribes during the Rif War. Spain relinquished the northern zone upon Moroccan independence in 1956 and ceded the southern Cape Juby sector in April 1958. \n\n Status: Protectorate of Spain; Capital: Tétouan; Official languages: Spanish; Common languages: Moroccan Arabic, Berber languages and Haketia; Religion: Sunni Islam and Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial protectorate; Ruler title: High Commissioner; Established: 27 November 1912; Disestablished: 1 April 1958; Currency: Spanish peseta

name: Provisional Government of Albania
description: The Provisional Government of Albania was formed at Vlorë on 28 November 1912 by national delegates who declared independence from the crumbling Ottoman Empire during the First Balkan War. Chaired by statesman Ismail Qemali, the nascent assembly created the country's first ministries, sought diplomatic recognition from the Great Powers and attempted to maintain domestic order amid ongoing regional conflicts. name: Republic of Central Albania

name: Division of the North
description: The Division of the North was the autonomous revolutionary army and territorial government commanded by General Francisco "Pancho" Villa during the Mexican Revolution. Based in the city of Chihuahua, the Villistas governed large portions of northern Mexico, printing their own currency, administering confiscated ranches and funding public welfare initiatives. name: Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria

Administered from Lagos under Governor-General Frederick Lugard, the British regime established a system of indirect rule that utilised traditional emirs and chiefs to supervise rural districts. name: Principality of Albania
description: The Principality of Albania was a sovereign constitutional monarchy established by the European Great Powers following the 1913 Treaty of London, with German Prince Wilhelm of Wied arriving to assume the throne in February 1914. Administered initially from Durrës and later Tirana, the new monarchy was quickly overwhelmed by local uprisings, tribal disputes and competing foreign military incursions during the First World War. name: Autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus
description: The Autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus was a self-declared Greek state proclaimed at Gjirokastër on 28 February 1914 by local Greek communities opposing their incorporation into newly established Albania. Chaired by former Greek foreign minister Georgios Christakis-Zografos, the provisional government organised militia units and negotiated broad self-governing rights under the Protocol of Corfu. name: Liberation Army of the South

Operating from its base at Tlaltizapán in Morelos, the movement fought under the principles of the Plan de Ayala to reclaim ancestral village lands from sugar hacienda owners. name: Uryankhay Krai
description: Uryankhay Krai was a protectorate established by the Russian Empire over Tuva on 14 April 1914, following petitions from local tribal nobility after the disintegration of the Qing dynasty. Administered from the newly founded town of Belotsarsk, the territory was supervised by a Russian commissar who regulated commercial timber, mining and trade while leaving Buddhist monastic authority intact. name: Territory of Norfolk Island

Administered from its historic settlement at Kingston, the island was formally transferred from British colonial oversight to Australian federal authority on 1 July 1914. The local population, largely descended from the Pitcairn Islanders and Bounty mutineers, maintained their distinctive Norfuk language and traditions while functioning under direct Australian Commonwealth administration. \n\n Status: External territory of Australia; Capital: Kingston; Official languages: English and Norfuk; Religion: Christianity; Government: Devolved dependency under territorial administrator; Ruler title: British monarch; Historical era: Modern era; Established: 1 July 1914; Currency: Australian dollar

name: General Council of Albania

Coordinated by traditional elders, Islamic scholars and Ottoman sympathisers across central Albania, the council demanded the restoration of Muslim governance and closer ties to Istanbul. name: German East Africa (Military Occupation)

Commanded by Colonel Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, German colonial forces, including thousands of indigenous askari soldiers, advanced across the Kenyan frontier and seized Taveta in August 1914 to interrupt British communication routes.
