name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland and French Republic (Military Occupation)
description: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland and French Republic (Military Occupation) was a joint Allied military administration established over the German protectorate of Togoland following its capitulation in August 1914. Coordinated by British and French officers operating from neighbouring Gold Coast and Dahomey, the authorities established a military condominium to maintain public order, cocoa production and coastal trade. name: Dominion of New Zealand (Military Occupation)
description: The Dominion of New Zealand (Military Occupation) commenced on 29 August 1914 when an expeditionary force from New Zealand landed at Apia and seized German Samoa without encountering resistance. Operating on behalf of the British Empire, New Zealand military authorities administered the Pacific archipelago throughout the First World War, maintaining public health, schools and local shipping. The military regime concluded in December 1920 when the League of Nations granted New Zealand a formal mandate over the territory. \n\n Status: Military occupation zone; Capital: Apia; Common languages: English, Samoan and German; Religion: Christianity; Government: Military administration; Ruler title: King; Historical era: World War I; Established: 29 August 1914; Disestablished: 17 December 1920; Succeeded by: Western Samoa

name: Constitutionalist Army
description: The Constitutionalist Army was the dominant revolutionary faction in Mexico organised by Venustiano Carranza following the overthrow of President Francisco I. Madero. Operating from Mexico City under military commanders such as Álvaro Obregón, the Constitutionalists defeated rival forces of Pancho Villa and Emiliano Zapata to secure national control. The movement drafted the landmark Constitution of 1917, enacting extensive social rights and national resource sovereignty before internal rivalries fractured the leadership in 1920. \n\n Status: Autonomous revolutionary faction; Capital: Mexico City; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Revolutionary constitutional government; Head of state: First Chief; Ruler title: First Chief; Historical era: Mexican Revolution; Established: 1 September 1914; Disestablished: 22 July 1920

name: Austria-Hungary and German Empire (Military Occupation)

name: Commonwealth of Australia (Military Occupation)

Operating across the disputed frontier without a permanent civilian seat, German colonial units commanded by Major Viktor Franke occupied Portuguese outposts and repelled Allied detachments. name: Sultanate of Egypt

Governed from Cairo with Hussein Kamel and later Fuad I installed as sultans, domestic affairs operated alongside an all-powerful British high commissioner who turned the country into a major Allied base. Headed by Ahmad Sharif as-Senussi from the religious sanctuary of Jaghbub, the Muslim revivalist brotherhood mobilised Bedouin tribesmen to wage resistance against Italian colonial forces and British frontier garrisons. name: Provisional Government of Van
description: The Provisional Government of Van was an autonomous self-defence administration organised by Armenian civic and political leaders in the city of Van on 19 April 1915. Formed to protect local Armenian communities from massacres by Ottoman military units and irregular cavalry, the administration was headed by Aram Manukian. name: Union of South Africa (Military Occupation)
description: The Union of South Africa (Military Occupation) comprised the operational martial regime established across conquered German South West Africa following the military campaign led by Generals Louis Botha and Jan Smuts. Operating without a civilian capital, South African military authorities administered strategic transport networks, police garrisons and diamond mining concessions throughout the former German territory. description: The French Republic and United Kingdom (Military Occupation) was a joint Allied military administration established over the German protectorate of Kamerun during the First World War. Following coordinated offensives by British, French and Belgian-colonial expeditionary units that pushed German defenders southward, the Allied commanders instituted a martial condominium to supervise conquered coastal and inland districts. name: Empire of China

Governed from Beijing, the regime intended to consolidate central authority and stabilise national finances by resurrecting traditional imperial ritualism within a constitutional framework. name: Emirate of Nejd and Hasa

Under this agreement, the British Empire recognised Ibn Saud's hereditary sovereignty over Nejd and the Persian Gulf coastline of al-Ahsa while providing monthly financial subsidies and arms shipments to counter the pro-Ottoman Emirate of Jabal Shammar. description: British Cameroons was a colonial territory in West Africa formed on 4 March 1916 following the joint Anglo-French conquest of German Kamerun during the First World War. Administered from Buea, the long narrow strip of territory comprised Northern Cameroons and Southern Cameroons and was administered as a League of Nations mandate and subsequent United Nations trust territory alongside colonial Nigeria. name: French Cameroon

Governed from Yaoundé, the territory was confirmed as a League of Nations Class B mandate in 1922 and transitioned into a United Nations trust territory within the French Union. French authorities promoted infrastructure projects, cocoa farming and coffee production while facing rising nationalist demands from the Union of the Peoples of Cameroon, culminating in full national independence in January 1960. \n\n Status: League of Nations mandate; Capital: Yaoundé; Official languages: French; Common languages: Ewondo, Basaa, Bulu and Fula; Religion: Christianity, Islam and traditional beliefs; Government: Colonial administration; Ruler title: President of France; Established: 4 March 1916; Disestablished: 1 January 1960; Currency: CFA franc

name: Kingdom of Belgium (Military Occupation)
description: The Kingdom of Belgium (Military Occupation) comprised foreign territories administered under martial law by the Belgian armed forces during and after both World Wars. Following campaigns in German East Africa that seized Rwanda and Burundi in May 1916, Belgian forces also participated in the Allied occupation of the German Rhineland and the Ruhr district during the 1920s to enforce reparations payments. In 1941, Belgian colonial units briefly occupied areas in East Africa during the liberation of Ethiopia from Italian control, maintaining order until civil administration was restored. \n\n Status: Military occupation zone; Capital: None (decentralised); Official languages: French and Dutch; Common languages: German, Kinyarwanda and Kirundi; Religion: Roman Catholicism and Lutheranism; Government: Military command; Ruler title: King of the Belgians; Established: 6 May 1916; Disestablished: 27 November 1941

name: Chinese Warlords

Operating without an effective central authority, rival Beiyang military cliques such as the Zhili, Anhui and Fengtian factions battled for possession of Beijing, while autonomous militarists dominated Sichuan, Yunnan and Guangdong. name: Kingdom of Hejaz
description: The Kingdom of Hejaz was an independent Hashemite state proclaimed on 10 June 1916 when Hussein bin Ali, the Sharif of Mecca, launched the Great Arab Revolt against the Ottoman Empire. Supported by British military and naval aid, Hashemite forces expelled Ottoman garrisons from the holy cities of Mecca and Medina and advanced northward along the Hejaz railway into Syria. name: Republic of Nicaragua

Administered from Managua, consecutive administrations operated under the close supervision of United States Marines who guarded public order, supervised customs receipts and directed the national bank. name: Central Powers (Military Occupation)
description: The Central Powers (Military Occupation) designated the joint martial administration established across occupied Romania following the decisive offensives of the German, Austro-Hungarian, Bulgarian and Ottoman armies in late 1916. Headed by German Field Marshal August von Mackensen from Bucharest, the occupational authority controlled Wallachia, Dobruja and strategic oil facilities around Ploiești to supply the wartime requirements of the Quadruple Alliance. name: Sheikhdom of Qatar
description: The Sheikhdom of Qatar became a formal British protectorate on 3 November 1916 when Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani signed a treaty of protection with the United Kingdom following the departure of Ottoman garrisons. Governed from the coastal settlement of Doha, the agreement ensured British naval defence against maritime attacks in exchange for Qatari adherence to imperial foreign policy and anti-piracy covenants. The protectorate oversaw the transformation of the country from a pearling economy into a wealthy petroleum exporter before declaring full independence in September 1971. \n\n Status: British protectorate; Capital and largest city: Doha; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Traditional monarchy under colonial protectorate; Ruling dynasty: House of Thani; Ruler title: Sheikh; Established: 3 November 1916; Disestablished: 3 September 1971; Currency: Qatari riyal

name: Autonomous Albanian Republic of Korçë
description: The Autonomous Albanian Republic of Korçë was an autonomous administrative entity established in southeastern Albania on 10 December 1916 by a convention between local Albanian leaders and French military forces. Governed from Korçë under the French military umbrella with Themistokli Gërmenji serving as police prefect, the republic introduced Albanian-language schooling, published native newspapers and raised an Albanian flag bearing the French tricolour. The French high command modified this autonomous protocol in early 1918 before progressively integrating the district back into Allied military administration as the First World War concluded. \n\n Status: French protectorate; Capital: Korçë; Official languages: Albanian and French; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy and Sunni Islam; Government: Autonomous municipal council under military protectorate; Ruler title: Prefect of Police; Historical era: World War I; Established: 10 December 1916; Disestablished: 16 February 1918; Currency: Korçë frange

name: British Togoland
description: British Togoland was a colonial territory in West Africa created on 27 December 1916 when Britain and France formally partitioned the former German protectorate of Togoland into separate administrative zones. Governed from Ho, the territory was subsequently confirmed as a League of Nations Class B mandate and later as a United Nations trust territory administered alongside the Gold Coast. Functioning as a Polish puppet buffer state, the administration governed a multi-ethnic region comprising Poles, Lithuanians, Belarusians and Jews under military martial law. Comprising the strategic Adriatic port city of Fiume and its immediate rural hinterland, the state was formed to resolve intractable territorial rivalries following the expulsion of Gabriele d'Annunzio's legionnaires. Placed under the direct protection and oversight of a League of Nations High Commissioner, the predominantly German-populated city-state maintained its own bicameral parliament, police force and currency. Operating from Yerevan, the early Soviet administration faced extreme famine, thousands of war refugees and the brief anti-communist February Uprising before stabilising under Aleksandr Myasnikyan. Headquartered at Apia on the island of Upolu, the New Zealand administration instituted direct colonial rule that sparked widespread non-violent resistance through the indigenous Mau movement. Confronted by expansionist pressure from the neighbouring Saudi Emirate of Nejd, the sheikhdom entered into a defensive protectorate alignment with King Hussein of Hejaz in 1921. Directed by the Georgian Revolutionary Committee under Filipp Makharadze, the fledgling Bolshevik administration suppressed remaining democratic institutions and integrated Georgian armed formations into the Soviet military hierarchy. description: The Albona Republic was proclaimed on 2 March 1921 by striking coal miners in the Istrian mining community of Labin. Formed in direct resistance to rising Italian Fascist violence and deteriorating labour conditions under Italian administration, the council established self-managed pit committees, organised an armed "red guard" militia and halted coal shipments. name: Republic of Costa Rica (Military Occupation)
description: The Republic of Costa Rica established a military occupation regime across the disputed Coto river valley and adjacent Pacific frontier sectors in March 1921 during the Coto War against Panama. Mobilised by presidential decree following years of demarcation disagreements, Costa Rican armed detachments seized military control of Pueblo Nuevo de Coto and advanced towards the Almirante gulf. name: Autonomous Government of Khorasan
description: The Autonomous Government of Khorasan was established in Mashhad on 2 April 1921 by Colonel Mohammad Taqi Khan Pessian, head of the provincial gendarmerie, in defiance of the central Qajar government in Tehran. Operating as a progressive military administration, Pessian instituted agrarian reforms, reduced consumer taxes and tackled administrative corruption throughout northeastern Iran. name: Emirate of Transjordan
description: The Emirate of Transjordan was established on 11 April 1921 as an autonomous Arab principality under the overarching framework of the British Mandate for Palestine. Governed from Amman by Hashemite prince Abdullah I bin Hussein under the supervision of a British High Commissioner, the polity maintained separate legal, financial and administrative institutions distinct from western Palestine. name: Republic of Mountainous Armenia

description: The Republic of Mountainous Armenia was proclaimed in Goris on 26 April 1921 by military commander Garegin Nzhdeh to defend the historic Syunik highland region against Soviet and Azerbaijani incursions. Mobilising seasoned fedayeen guerrillas and local Armenian villagers, the anti-Bolshevik state tenaciously held rugged mountain passes and prevented the annexation of Zangezur to Soviet Azerbaijan. name: Jabal Druze State
description: The Jabal Druze State was created on 1 May 1921 by French mandatory authorities to provide an autonomous homeland for the Druze population of the southern Hauran plateau. Headquartered at As-Suwayda and governed under direct French oversight through traditional clan notables, the state was designed to weaken broad Syrian Arab nationalism by fostering communal particularism. name: Provisional Government of the Priamur

description: The Provisional Government of the Priamur was established in Vladivostok on 26 May 1921 following an anti-Bolshevik coup supported by Japanese occupation forces. Directed initially by merchant Spiridon Merkulov and subsequently by General Mikhail Diterikhs as a traditionalist Zemsky Krai, the state served as the final White Russian redoubt during the civil war. name: Serb-Hungarian Baranya-Baja Republic
description: The Serb-Hungarian Baranya-Baja Republic was proclaimed in Pécs on 14 August 1921 by left-wing political figures and ethnic minority representatives headed by painter Petar Dobrović. Occupying the southernmost tier of Hungary under the temporary military protection of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, the short-lived council sought to protect local democratic and socialist elements from the White Terror of Admiral Horthy's regime. Operating from the capital city of Kyzyl under the guidance of the Tuvan People's Revolutionary Party, the state functioned as a dependent Soviet satellite while maintaining nominal international independence recognised only by Moscow and Ulaanbaatar. name: Confederal Republic of the Tribes of the Rif
description: The Confederal Republic of the Tribes of the Rif was founded on 18 September 1921 at Ajdir following the historic Berber victory over Spanish colonial troops at the Battle of Annual. Led by jurist and guerrilla strategist Abd el-Krim, the confederation unified contentious Riffian and Jebala clans into a centralised Islamic republic equipped with modern artillery, telephone networks and judicial courts. The breakaway state resisted massive colonial offensives until a combined Franco-Spanish expeditionary force of over two hundred thousand men, supported by aerial chemical bombardments, forced Abd el-Krim's surrender in May 1926. \n\n Status: Unrecognised confederal republic; Capital: Ajdir; Official languages: Arabic; Common languages: Tarifit and Jebli Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Confederal Islamic republic; Ruler title: President; Head of state: Abd el-Krim; Historical era: Rif War; Established: 18 September 1921; Disestablished: 30 May 1926; Preceded by: Spanish Morocco; Succeeded by: Spanish Morocco; Currency: Riffan

name: Republic of Finland (Military Occupation)
description: The Republic of Finland established military occupation administrations across sections of Eastern Karelia during regional border conflicts and the Continuation War. Between December 1921 and February 1922, Finnish volunteer forces occupied northern Karelian districts during an anti-Soviet insurrection, seeking to support fellow Finno-Ugric populations before being expelled by regular Red Army columns. name: Comoros
description: The Comoros functioned as a French colonial dependency in the Mozambique Channel from 1922, initially administered as a province attached to the government-general of Madagascar. Incorporating the four principal volcanic islands of Grande Comore, Anjouan, Mohéli and Mayotte, colonial authorities alienated extensive fertile lands to private concession companies for vanilla, ylang-ylang and perfume-crop production. Reorganised as an autonomous French overseas territory after the Second World War with its administrative seat at Moroni, the archipelago pursued progressive self-governance until declaring sovereign independence in July 1975. \n\n Status: French overseas territory; Capital: Moroni; Official languages: French; Common languages: Comorian and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Colonial dependency; Ruler title: High Commissioner; Historical era: Decolonisation era; Established: 1 January 1922; Disestablished: 6 July 1975; Preceded by: Madagascar and Dependencies; Succeeded by: Union of the Comoros; Currency: Comorian franc

description: The French Republic and the Kingdom of Belgium maintained a joint military occupation across Germany's Ruhr industrial heartland and adjacent Rhineland sectors between 1922 and 1926. Initiated to enforce the payment of war reparations under the Treaty of Versailles following German defaults in coal and timber shipments, the occupation saw Franco-Belgian army divisions seize railway networks, metallurgical mills and coal mines. Governed through naval administrators in cooperation with the British Phosphate Commission, the isolated Micronesian island was prized almost exclusively for its immense, high-grade phosphate deposits. name: Sultanate of Nejd
description: The Sultanate of Nejd was established across the central Arabian plateau after Abdulaziz ibn Saud conquered the rival Emirate of Jabal Shammar and adopted the title of Sultan in late 1921. Linked to Great Britain through the Treaty of Darin and subsequent frontier demarcations arranged at the 1922 Uqair Conference, the sultanate maintained a powerful Bedouin fighting force driven by the zealous Ikhwan fraternity. Operating from his ancestral seat at Riyadh, Ibn Saud launched decisive military campaigns against the neighbouring Hashemite Kingdom of Hejaz, completing the conquest of the holy cities in December 1925. \n\n Status: British-protected sultanate; Capital: Riyadh; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute Islamic monarchy; Ruling dynasty: House of Saud; Ruler title: Sultan; Head of state: Abdulaziz ibn Saud; Historical era: Interwar period; Established: 1 January 1922; Disestablished: 19 December 1925; Preceded by: Emirate of Nejd and Hasa; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd; Currency: Maria Theresa thaler

name: Kingdom of Egypt
description: The Kingdom of Egypt was established on 28 February 1922 when Great Britain issued a unilateral declaration terminating its wartime protectorate and Sultan Fuad I assumed the royal title. Headquartered in Cairo and operating under the liberal 1923 Constitution, the kingdom featured a vibrant parliamentary life contested between the nationalist Wafd Party and the royal palace. Centred administratively in Tbilisi, the regional federation was established under Bolshevik guidance to coordinate economic reconstruction, manage Caspian petroleum resources and resolve bitter inter-ethnic disputes across the South Caucasus. description: The Provisional Yakut Regional People's Government was formed in Churapcha on 23 March 1922 by indigenous Yakut intellectuals and White Russian military officers during the final stages of the Russian Civil War. Sparked by intense local resistance to Bolshevik grain requisitions and Soviet administrative centralisation, the rebel government raised the Yakut People's Army and welcomed General Anatoly Pepelyayev's expeditionary White force. The insurgency controlled wide expanses of northeastern Siberia until winter campaigns by the Red Army dispersed the insurgent detachments by late December 1922. \n\n Status: Unrecognised insurgent government; Capital: Churapcha; Common languages: Yakut and Russian; Religion: Russian Orthodoxy and Shamanism; Government: Provisional regional government; Ruler title: Chairman; Head of state: Pyotr Kulakovsky; Historical era: Russian Civil War; Established: 23 March 1922; Disestablished: 30 December 1922; Preceded by: Russian SFSR; Succeeded by: Russian SFSR

description: The Syrian Federation was established on 28 June 1922 by French High Commissioner Henri Gouraud, uniting the autonomous states of Damascus, Aleppo and the Alawites into a unified federal framework. Directed by a Federal Council under President Subhi Bey Barakat that alternated its meetings between Aleppo and Damascus, the arrangement reflected a cautious French initiative to streamline colonial administration and conciliate moderate nationalist demands. name: Kingdom of Kurdistan
description: The Kingdom of Kurdistan was proclaimed in Sulaymaniyah on 1 October 1922 when influential Kurdish religious leader Mahmud Barzanji declared himself King of Kurdistan in the wake of the Ottoman collapse. Mobilising tribal militias across southern Kurdistan, the monarchist government created an administrative cabinet, raised Kurdish flags and collected regional customs duties in open defiance of the British Mandate of Mesopotamia. name: Colony of Niger
description: The Colony of Niger was created on 13 October 1922 when French colonial authorities transformed the Military Territory of Niger into a civilian constituent colony of French West Africa. Governed initially from the southern trading city of Zinder before transferring the colonial capital to Niamey on the Niger River in 1926, the administration governed vast desert expanses by co-opting Hausa, Zarma and Tuareg traditional chiefs. name: Saudi-Kuwaiti Neutral Zone

Encompassing an undivided diamond of desert terrain along the Persian Gulf, the condominium granted the Sultanate of Nejd and the Sheikhdom of Kuwait completely equal rights over land use, pasturage and mineral wealth without establishing a civil administrative capital. name: Irish Free State
description: The Irish Free State was established on 6 December 1922 pursuant to the Anglo-Irish Treaty, which concluded the Irish War of Independence and constituted twenty-six counties of Ireland as a self-governing Dominion within the British Empire. Headquartered in Dublin with King George V represented by a Governor-General, the new state immediately endured a bitter ten-month civil war against anti-treaty republicans before stabilising under President of the Executive Council W. T. Cosgrave. description: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was founded on 30 December 1922 through the formal treaty of union uniting the Russian, Ukrainian, Byelorussian and Transcaucasian Soviet republics. Headquartered at the Moscow Kremlin and ideologically grounded in Marxist-Leninist communism, the federal superpower transformed a war-torn agrarian empire into a nuclear-armed industrial giant through centralised five-year plans and comprehensive state control. name: Colony of Southern Rhodesia
description: The Colony of Southern Rhodesia was formally constituted on 12 September 1923 when the British Crown annexed the chartered territories of the British South Africa Company south of the Zambezi River. Operating from Salisbury as a self-governing Crown colony, the administration was dominated by a prosperous white minority electorate that enacted restrictive land-apportionment laws and disenfranchised the indigenous African majority. name: Autonomous Palatinate
description: The Autonomous Palatinate was proclaimed in Speyer on 10 October 1923 by regional separatist leader Franz Josef Heinz during the crisis of the French occupation of the Rhineland. Encouraged by French occupation officers seeking to detach western German provinces from the Weimar Republic, Heinz's armed Free Corps seized municipal halls across Kaiserslautern, Pirmasens and Speyer. Closely aligned with the Soviet Union throughout its existence, the pastoral nation transformed its nomadic social structure under the Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party through state collectivisation, the secularisation of Buddhist monasteries and industrial development.
